chapters.title: Chapter 1: What TDS Is and How It Works

lessons.title: Deductor, Deductee, TAN and PAN: The Players and Terms You Need

body.text: Every TDS entry is a link between two ID numbers: the deductor's TAN and your PAN. If either one is missing or wrong, the tax can be sitting safely with the government and still never reach your account.

children.text: Rohan is a 29-year-old product analyst in Hyderabad. When he opened his Annual Information Statement for the first time, he found four different organisations had deducted tax from him in one year: his employer, HDFC Bank, a Nifty 50 company whose shares he holds, and a Bengaluru startup he did weekend consulting for. Each entry carried a strange 10-character code he had never seen before, next to his own PAN.

That code was a TAN. To read your own TDS records, check them and fix them when they go wrong, you need to know who the players are, what each one is responsible for, and what the two identification numbers actually tell you.
The Deductor: Who Has to Cut the Tax

markDefs.definition: The person or organisation that makes a payment and is legally required to withhold tax from it and deposit that tax with the government.

children.text: The
deductor
is whoever makes the payment. The law places the duty on the payer because the payer controls the money. But not every payer is a deductor. The rules depend on who is paying and for what.

cells: Companies, LLPs, partnership firms, trusts, government bodies
Yes, on every payment type covered by the law, once the threshold is crossed
Your employer, your bank, a company paying you dividends, a startup paying your consulting fee
Individuals and HUFs whose business or profession needs a tax audit
Yes, broadly the same as a business
A trader or doctor whose turnover or receipts cross the tax audit limit
All other individuals and HUFs, including most salaried people
Only in a few specific cases
Paying rent above ₹50,000 a month (2%), buying property worth ₹50,00,000 or more (1%), paying a contractor or professional more than ₹50,00,000 in a year (2%)

children.text: So a salaried person who pays a chartered accountant to file their return, a plumber to fix a leak or a tutor for their child does not deduct TDS. But the same person becomes a deductor the day they sign a flat purchase agreement for ₹60 lakh.

body.title: Quick Check: Deductor or Not?
body.question: Which of these people is required to deduct TDS on the payment described?
options: Sneha, a salaried HR manager in Pune, paying her CA ₹25,000 for filing her return
Vikram, a salaried engineer in Noida, paying ₹65,000 a month rent for his flat
Anjali, a salaried teacher in Kolkata, paying a carpenter ₹1,80,000 to make furniture
Farhan, a salaried banker in Mumbai, buying a used car for ₹7,00,000
body.explanation: Individuals who are not under tax audit only deduct in a handful of cases. Rent above ₹50,000 a month is one of them, so Vikram must deduct 2%. Sneha's and Anjali's payments are far below the ₹50,00,000 annual limit for contractor and professional payments by individuals, and buying a used car is not a TDS event for the buyer at all.

children.text: What a deductor has to do

cells: Apply for a Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number before the first deduction
Withhold tax at the right rate when the payment is made or credited, whichever is earlier
Pay the tax to the government, quoting the TAN
By the 7th of the next month (30 April for March)
Report each deductee's PAN, amount paid and tax deducted. Salary TDS goes in Form 138 (formerly Form 24Q), most other resident payments in Form 140 (formerly Form 26Q)
Give each deductee proof of the deduction. Salary: Form 130 (formerly Form 16). Other payments: Form 131 (formerly Form 16A)
Form 130 once a year by 15 June. Form 131 every quarter

body.text: Look at who carries the risk. Interest for late deduction or deposit, penalties for missing statements and the disallowance of business expenses all fall on the deductor. The law deliberately puts the pressure on the party holding the money.

children.text: The Deductee: Your Side of the Deal

markDefs.definition: The person who receives a payment from which tax has been deducted. The tax is treated as paid on this person's behalf and is credited against their PAN.

children.text: The
deductee
is you, the person receiving the money. Your duties are lighter, but they are not optional.

columns.label: Deductor
points: Holds a TAN and quotes it on every deposit and statement
Deducts at the correct rate and deposits on time
Reports your PAN and the amounts correctly every quarter
Corrects its statement if it made a mistake

columns.label: Deductee (you)
points: Gives your correct PAN to every payer before the payment
Keeps your PAN operative by linking it with Aadhaar
Checks Form 26AS and AIS to confirm every credit appears
Reports the gross income in your return, not the amount received
Claims the TDS credit and chases the deductor if something is missing

body.text: If tax has actually been deducted from your payment, the department cannot demand that same tax from you directly, even if the deductor never deposited it. This protection sits in Section 401 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 205). In practice you still need proof of the deduction, such as payslips or a TDS certificate, so keep them.

children.text: TAN: The Deductor's ID

markDefs.definition: Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number. A 10-character alphanumeric number that every person required to deduct or collect tax at source must obtain and quote on TDS deposits, statements and certificates.

children.text: A
TAN

is to TDS what a PAN is to income tax. The obligation to obtain one sits in Section 397(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 203A). It always has the same shape: four letters, five digits, one letter.

cells: Code for the city or region where the TAN was allotted, here Mumbai
First letter of the deductor's name, for example Shree Ganesh Textiles
Unique number generated by the system
Check letter generated by the system

children.text: Businesses apply online through the Protean (formerly NSDL) portal. The long-familiar application was Form 49B, and the processing fee is ₹65 including GST. Under the Income-tax Rules, 2026, the TAN application has been renumbered, reportedly as Form 135 for non-government deductors. Failing to obtain a TAN when required, or quoting a wrong one, can attract a penalty of ₹10,000.

body.text: Individuals who deduct only on rent, property purchases, large contractor payments or crypto transfers do not need a TAN. They deposit the tax and report it in one go using their own PAN, through Form 141, which replaces the old Forms 26QB, 26QC, 26QD and 26QE.

children.text: PAN: Your ID, and Why Every Character Counts

markDefs.definition: Permanent Account Number. A 10-character alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department that links all of a person's tax records, including TDS credits.

children.text: Your
PAN
has the pattern five letters, four digits, one letter. Two of those letters carry meaning you can read at a glance.

cells: Alphabetic series allotted by the department
Type of holder. P is an individual
For individuals, the first letter of the surname. For others, the first letter of the entity's name

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Whose PAN Is This?
body.textWithBlank: A dividend payment is reported against PAN AABCT1234Q. The 4th character tells you this PAN belongs to a ___.
body.explanation: The 4th character is C, which stands for company. If you ever see a PAN like this against income that should be yours, the payer has reported it under the wrong PAN.

children.text: The reason the deductor asks for your PAN is simple: without it, the system cannot put the credit in your name, so the law makes the missing PAN expensive. Under Section 397(2) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 206AA), if you do not furnish a valid PAN, TDS is generally deducted at the higher of the normal rate or 20%.

body.title: Try It: The Cost of Not Sharing Your PAN
body.prompt: Ishita, a freelance content writer in Jaipur, sends a Delhi agency an invoice for ₹80,000 in professional fees but forgets to share her PAN. Normal TDS is 10%. How much extra tax is deducted because of the missing PAN?
body.explanation: With a PAN, TDS is 10% of ₹80,000 = ₹8,000. Without one, it is 20% = ₹16,000. The extra ₹8,000 is not lost forever, but it is locked up until she files her return, and because the credit is not tagged to her PAN, claiming it becomes difficult. Sharing her PAN with the invoice would have avoided the whole problem.

body.text: An inoperative PAN is treated as no PAN at all. A PAN becomes inoperative if it is not linked with Aadhaar by the applicable deadline, and TDS then jumps to the higher rate even though you shared the number. Lesson 2 of Chapter 4 covers how to check and fix this.

children.text: Putting Names to Rohan's Statement
Here is what Rohan saw in the TDS section of his AIS for tax year 2026-27, with every player now identifiable. The TANs are illustrative.

cells: His employer, a Hyderabad IT company

body.title: Where Rohan's ₹1,12,140 of TDS came from

children.text: Rohan's employer deducted ₹88,140 on the assumption that salary was his only income: ₹14,40,000 less the ₹75,000 standard deduction under the new regime, taxed at slab rates plus 4% cess. The other three deductors had no idea about each other. Only Rohan, looking at the full statement, can see the whole picture, and Chapter 5 shows him how to use it.

body.title: Scenario: The Missing Salary TDS
body.scenario: Deepa, a nurse at a private hospital in Chennai, checks her Form 26AS in June. Her payslips show ₹54,000 of income tax deducted over the year, but her statement shows no salary TDS at all. HR confirms the tax was deposited every month. On closer inspection, the Form 130 her employer issued lists her PAN with two digits swapped.
body.prompt: Why is the credit missing, who has to fix it, and what should Deepa do before she files her return?
body.modelAnswer: The tax was deposited under the hospital's TAN, but the quarterly salary statement reported it against the wrong PAN, so the credit went nowhere useful, or to someone else. Only the deductor can fix this, by filing a correction statement for each affected quarter with her correct PAN. Deepa should write to HR with a copy of her PAN card, ask for corrections to all four quarterly statements, and ask for a revised Form 130. She should keep her payslips as proof that tax was deducted. Once the correction is processed, usually within a few weeks, the ₹54,000 should appear in Form 26AS and AIS, and she can file her return claiming the full credit. If she files before the correction shows up, the system may not allow the credit, so it is worth waiting if the deadline allows.

body.title: Salaried and paying rent above ₹50,000 a month? You are a deductor too

children.text: Vikram from the quiz pays ₹60,000 a month. Tenants who are individuals or HUFs not under tax audit deduct 2% on rent above ₹50,000 a month. Under the rules carried over from the old Section 194-IB, the deduction is generally made once, from the rent for the last month of the tax year or of the tenancy, on the total rent for that period.

content.caption: 12 months at ₹60,000, deducted from the March rent

children.text: So in March, Vikram pays his landlord ₹45,600 instead of ₹60,000, deposits ₹14,400 using Form 141 with his PAN within 30 days from the end of March, and gives the landlord a TDS certificate. No TAN is needed. Chapter 3 covers rent TDS in full, including what happens if the landlord has no PAN.
Check Your Own Players

body.title: Audit the IDs in Your Tax Records
steps: Confirm your PAN is operative: on the e-filing portal, use Link Aadhaar Status with your PAN and Aadhaar
Open your AIS and list every deductor name and TAN in the TDS section
Use the Know TAN Details service on the e-filing portal to confirm any deductor you do not recognise
Check the PAN printed on your latest Form 130 or Form 131 matches your PAN card character by character
Make sure your bank, broker and every client you invoice has your current PAN on record

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal
body.description: Pre-login services include Link Aadhaar Status and Know TAN Details. Log in to view AIS and Form 26AS.

cards.definition: The payer who withholds tax from a payment and deposits it with the government.
The person receiving the payment, whose PAN the TDS is credited to.
Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number. 10 characters in the pattern AAAA99999A, required for most deductors under Section 397(1), formerly 203A.
Permanent Account Number. 10 characters in the pattern AAAAA9999A. The 4th character shows the type of holder.
TDS certificate for salary, formerly Form 16. Issued once a year by the employer.
TDS certificate for non-salary payments, formerly Form 16A. Issued quarterly.
PAN-based challan-cum-statement used by individuals deducting on rent, property, large contractor payments and crypto, replacing Forms 26QB, 26QC, 26QD and 26QE.
Higher TDS, generally 20%, when a valid PAN is not furnished. Formerly Section 206AA.

points: The deductor is the payer and carries almost all the compliance burden: TAN, deduction, deposit, quarterly statements and certificates
Most salaried individuals only become deductors when paying rent above ₹50,000 a month, buying property worth ₹50,00,000 or more, or paying a contractor or professional over ₹50,00,000 in a year
TAN identifies the deductor (AAAA99999A). PAN identifies you (AAAAA9999A), and its 4th character shows the type of holder
Without a valid, operative PAN, TDS generally jumps to 20% under Section 397(2), formerly 206AA
If tax was deducted from you, the department cannot demand it from you again under Section 401, formerly 205, but keep proof
A single wrong PAN digit in the deductor's statement can make your credit disappear, and only the deductor can file the correction

Rates, thresholds, form numbers and provisions reflect the position understood at the time of writing and can change. Verify current rules on the Income Tax Department website or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
